ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: The last day of the twelfth month is both the calendar’s year-end and a Chan deadline for what cannot be deferred.
EvidenceBody: Dahui Zonggao asks what saying will meet birth and death then; Yunfeng raises Baizhang’s warning about how unprepared students will settle their account, and Zhe’an Jingfan describes conditions closing in.

Jifei Ruyi’s questioner uses the literal date, while Hongjue Min says there will be no time for idle talk, Wuzhun Shifan tests a year of words at its deadline, and Guyin Yuncong makes the date a direct answer about the Way.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: A fixed calendar date becomes the public deadline at which words, preparation, and claimed understanding must answer for themselves.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The date is not a prediction of one literal death-day; its death pressure is explicit in some cases, while other uses remain ordinary year-end observance.
